**Understanding your two seizures and what happens next**

You have had two generalised seizures within three months. A generalised seizure means a burst of abnormal electrical activity affecting the whole brain at once, usually causing loss of consciousness with shaking or stiffness. Two episodes in a short time makes it more likely that this is an ongoing tendency to seizures rather than a one-off event, but that is not yet confirmed — it is a working possibility, not a diagnosis.

At the moment, the records I can see do not include a detailed description of how each episode began, whether you had any warning, or how you felt afterwards. They also do not include any EEG (a test that records the brain's electrical signals) or MRI (a detailed scan of the brain's structure) reports, nor your background medical history or medicines. Importantly, this does not mean those tests were never done or were normal — the information simply is not available to me here. So I cannot yet tell you what the episodes mean, whether they were epilepsy, or whether anything was found on testing. That uncertainty is real, and it is why specialist follow-up matters.

The plan is for you to be reviewed by a specialist, who will go through your event history, any existing test results, and may arrange further tests if needed. They will discuss whether treatment is appropriate — I will not suggest any specific medicine here, as that decision belongs with them and with you.

In the meantime, practical safety matters: avoid situations where a sudden loss of consciousness could be dangerous, such as swimming alone, working at heights, or using dangerous machinery. For driving, please follow your local licensing rules and check with your treating team, since rules vary and they can advise you precisely.

I would also like to understand what matters most to you.

1. What are your biggest worries right now — safety, work or study, driving, or something else?
2. Do you remember anything about how each seizure started or how you felt before and after?
